lines: "comment": "Same coverage as the \"all\" entry above, but driven by ./configure --enable-cryptocb=only instead of a hand-written CPPFLAGS list. This is the regression test for the configure option: it must emit exactly the WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_ONLY_* set that \"all\" passes by hand, for the algorithms enabled here. The \"all\" entry deliberately stays on explicit CPPFLAGS so a bug in the configure logic cannot silently weaken both. Note the base already passes --enable-cryptocb; this entry's flags are appended after the base, so --enable-cryptocb=only wins.",

+           "comment": "WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_KEYGEN_SW_FALLBACK: an id or label key whose registered device declines key generation is generated in software again instead of failing with NO_VALID_DEVID. test_wc_ecc_make_key_id_dev checks that fallback here; every other entry builds the default, which refuses. No ONLY_* strip, so software key generation is available.",

"comment": "--enable-cryptocbutils enables all cryptocb utilities (COPY/FREE/SETKEY/EXPORT_KEY/KEYSTORE); WOLF_CRYPTO_CB_SETKEY is what lets test_wc_CryptoCb_TLS_CBC_HMAC run -- a TLS 1.2 CBC MtE handshake whose record HMAC is computed by a key-owning callback, the only config exercising the TLS_hmac update/final routing. No ONLY_* strip, so the device's software HMAC keeps its providers.",
